title: Colorado Turning Point USA Chapter Membership Stagnates Following Campus Taco Bell Incident
snippet: Enrollment for a Colorado Turning Point USA chapter has plateaued after a bizarre altercation where an elderly supporter was struck by a student throwing a Taco Bell cup.
content:
A Turning Point USA (TPUSA) chapter in Colorado is experiencing stagnant recruitment numbers following a bizarre campus altercation that left an elderly volunteer targeted during a promotional drive.

Controversy Drives Attention, But Not Enrollment

The incident occurred during a high-tension political engagement event on campus, where an elderly conservative activist supporting the chapter was allegedly struck by a student throwing a Taco Bell drink cup. While video clips and reports of the altercation quickly circulated across social media platforms, chapter organizers admit that the viral publicity has failed to translate into new student sign-ups, leaving membership numbers largely unchanged.

Navigating a Polarized Campus Climate

The altercation highlights the growing political tension surrounding conservative youth organizations on college campuses nationwide. While high-profile incidents often mobilize core supporters online, local political analysts observe that public confrontations can sometimes deter prospective members who fear social repercussions or safety concerns on campus. University officials confirmed they are reviewing safety protocols for student group tabling events to prevent similar physical altercations in the future.
